mainTopic: How far each of the two goats of יום הכפורים reaches: when the inner goat suspends punishment, why it does not fully atone, and why neither goat can take over the other's atonement
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the inner goat of יום הכפורים (שעיר הנעשה בפנים). The ברייתא asks for a source that the goat is תולה for someone who knew at the beginning but not at the end. The גמרא explains why this needed a source. Comparing חטאים to פשעים could be read strictly, so that the goat covers only sins that can never bring a קרבן. The verse "לכל חטאתם" shows that the inner goat is for people who will later owe a חטאת. The same wording shows the goat only suspends the punishment and does not fully atone. רבא explains that this suspension protects the person from יסורין. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's case of awareness only at the end. It asks whether either goat could take over the other's job, and answers from the words "אחת" and "אחת בשנה". That last answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse teaches that the goat does not even suspend punishment
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an earlier answer. Without the verse, we might have said the inner goat at least suspends the punishment. The verse teaches us that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You might have thought] it should at least hold off his punishment. So the verse teaches us [that it does not].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous lines. The verse was needed so we would not think the inner goat suspends punishment for a sin that brings its own personal קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked why the verse had to exclude such a sin from the goat's atonement. The answer is that we might have thought the goat is at least תולה until he brings his קרבן. 'קא משמע לן' tells us the verse rules even that out.

keyTerms.meaning: It should suspend (hold off) the punishment, from the word תּוֹלֶה
It teaches us. This shows what new idea a verse or teaching is adding

phrases.english: [You might think] it should suspend [the punishment] for him,
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the inner goat of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: [so the verse] teaches us [that it does not].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the answer from the previous section of the דף
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a sin that brings its own personal קרבן, the inner goat does not atone and does not even suspend the punishment.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks for a source that the goat suspends punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It asks how we know the inner goat suspends punishment when the person knew at the beginning but not at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: How do we know that when a person knew at the beginning but did not know at the end, this goat holds off his punishment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא it has been studying. The ברייתא asks for a source that the inner goat is תולה in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who knew he was טמא but later forgot and entered the מקדש or ate קדשים. He knew at the beginning but has not yet realized at the end. The ברייתא wants a source that the inner goat holds off his punishment until he finds out and brings his קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness at the beginning: he knew he was טמא before he sinned
Awareness at the end: he later realizes that he sinned
Goat. Here it means the inner goat of יום הכפורים, whose blood is brought inside
Suspends: it holds off the punishment but does not fully atone

phrases.english: The Master said:
From where [do we know] that where there was awareness at the beginning
but there was no awareness at the end
that this goat suspends [the punishment]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner goat is תולה for one who had ידיעה בתחילה but not ידיעה בסוף, and the ברייתא looks for a source for this.

steps.title: Why does this need a source at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the ברייתא asks 'מנין'. What made the ברייתא think this rule was hard enough to need a proof?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How do we know'?! What is bothering him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא felt it needed a source. The rule seemed simple, so what problem was the ברייתא trying to solve?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had just taught that the goat covers sins that are not בני קרבן right now, like this one. So it seems obvious the goat would at least suspend the punishment here. The גמרא asks what doubt made the ברייתא look for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? A request for a source
What is difficult for him? It asks what problem pushed the speaker to ask

phrases.english: "From where"?!
What is difficult for him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the author of the ברייתא. The גמרא wants to know why he needed a source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא in step 2 needed to ask for a source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What doubt led the ברייתא to think the goat might not be תולה in this case?

steps.title: The comparison to פשעים could be made stricter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's worry was this. If the goat only covers sins that resemble פשעים, maybe it only covers sins that can NEVER bring a קרבן. That would be someone who did not know at the beginning but knew at the end. Someone who knew at the beginning will bring a קרבן once he finds out, so maybe the goat should not even suspend his punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothers him: You said sins are like rebellions. Just as rebellions are not subject to a קרבן, the goat covers only sins that are not subject to a קרבן. But maybe say it more strictly: just as rebellions can never bring a קרבן, the goat covers only sins that can never bring a קרבן. Which sins are those? Where he did not know at the beginning but did know at the end. But where he knew at the beginning and did not know at the end, he will bring a קרבן once he finds out. So maybe the goat should not even hold off his punishment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's doubt. The comparison of חטאים to פשעים could be read more strictly, and that reading would leave out our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read the comparison. In the loose reading, 'not a בר קרבן' means not able to bring a קרבן right now, which includes our case. In the strict reading it means never able to bring one, which leaves out our case. This person will become a בר קרבן as soon as he remembers, so under the strict reading the goat might not even be תולה for him. That is why the ברייתא needed a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Unintentional sins
Rebellious, deliberate sins, which never bring a קרבן
Similar to, compared to
Subject to (able to bring) a קרבן for atonement
Ever, at any time. Here it means never, even in the future

steps.confusionAlert: In the case of 'awareness at the beginning but not at the end', the person did NOT know at the end. He forgot and has not realized he sinned yet. That is why he cannot bring a קרבן right now, but he will be able to once he finds out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a single comparison (חטאים like פשעים) can be stretched more or less widely. Deciding how far it reaches decides whether this whole case is covered by the inner goat.

phrases.english: This is what is difficult for him:
Now that you have said
[that the goat covers] sins similar to acts of rebellion —
just as acts of rebellion are not subject to an offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַטָּאִים נָמֵי דְּלָאו בְּנֵי קׇרְבָּן;
phrases.english: so too [it covers] sins that are not subject to an offering;
[why not] say:

phrases.aramaic: מָה פְּשָׁעִים דְּלָאו בְּנֵי קׇרְבָּן לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: just as acts of rebellion are never subject to an offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַטָּאִים דְּלָאו בְּנֵי קׇרְבָּן לְעוֹלָם;
phrases.english: so too [it covers only] sins that are never subject to an offering;
and what are they?
[Where] there was no awareness at the beginning
but there was awareness at the end;
but where there was awareness at the beginning
and no awareness at the end,
since when it becomes known to him
he is subject to an offering —
say that it should not even suspend [his punishment]!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ חֲטָאִים דּוּמְיָא דִּפְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by explaining what doubt pushed the ברייתא to ask 'מנין'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison to פשעים could be read as 'never a בר קרבן'. That reading would leave out one who knew at the beginning, since he becomes a בר קרבן once he finds out. So the goat might not even be תולה for him.

steps.title: A possible reply: the other case already has atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a possible pushback against the strict reading. The case of no awareness at the beginning but awareness at the end is already atoned for by the outer goat and by יום הכפורים itself. So the inner goat cannot be the one meant for that case. The next step answers this pushback.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: where he did not know at the beginning but knew at the end, the goat done outside and the day of יום הכפורים already atone [so the inner goat cannot be meant for that case];
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings a possible argument against the strict reading, and the reply to it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict reading said the inner goat covers only the case of no awareness at the beginning. But that case is already covered by the outer goat (שעיר הנעשה בחוץ) and by יום הכפורים. So there would be no reason for the inner goat to cover it. If this argument works, the strict reading falls apart and we are back to the original question of why the ברייתא needed a source.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. It introduces a possible argument that the גמרא will then respond to
The goat whose service is done outside: the מוסף goat of יום הכפורים, offered on the outer מזבח
The day of יום הכפורים itself brings atonement

phrases.english: And if you would say:
[where] there was no awareness at the beginning
but there was awareness at the end —
the goat whose service is performed outside
and יום הכפורים [itself] atone;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא: אֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible argument against the strict reading proposed in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The strict reading that the inner goat covers only sins that are 'never בני קרבן'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case the strict reading leaves for the inner goat is already atoned for by the outer goat and יום הכפורים, so the inner goat would have nothing to add there.
steps.kashyaTarget: The strict reading from step 4, that the inner goat covers only sins that are 'never בני קרבן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case the strict reading leaves for the inner goat (no awareness at the beginning, awareness at the end) is already atoned for by the outer goat and יום הכפורים, so the inner goat would add nothing there.

steps.title: The verse stops us from swapping the two goats
steps.stepSummary: One might have reversed which goat covers which case, so the verse "לכל חטאתם" is needed. It shows the inner goat is for people who would bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we should flip it around. So the verse says "for all their sins," which shows these are people who would bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback from the last step. It explains why the ברייתא still needed a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pushback said the outer goat already covers 'no awareness at the beginning, awareness at the end,' so the inner goat cannot be meant for that case. The answer is that without a verse, we might have swapped the two goats: the inner goat for that case and the outer goat for someone who knew at the beginning. The words "לכל חטאתם" stop this swap, because they show the inner goat is for people who will later owe a חטאת. That means someone who knew at the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say (what we might have thought)
Let us reverse it, flip the cases around
"For all their sins" (ויקרא 16:16)
People who are fit to bring a sin-offering

steps.confusionAlert: Here "חטאתם" is read as connected to the קרבן חטאת, the sin-offering. It is not just a general word for sins.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say
that we should reverse it,
phrases.notes: He means swapping which goat, the inner or the outer, covers which case.

phrases.english: so the verse says: "For all their sins"
which shows that these are people who would bring sin-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a הוה אמינא of swapping the goats made the proof necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inner goat might cover 'no awareness at the beginning' and the outer goat might cover 'awareness at the beginning.'
steps.terutzMaskana: "לכל חטאתם" ties the inner goat to people who will owe a חטאת, meaning those who knew at the beginning.

steps.title: Why not give full atonement?
steps.stepSummary: If the inner goat covers this person, why should it only suspend his punishment? Let it atone completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it give him complete atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling that the goat only suspends punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the inner goat applies to this person, it seems odd that it does only half the job. Why not wipe out the sin fully, so he would not have to bring a קרבן later?

keyTerms.meaning: Complete atonement
Suspends (holds off the punishment for now)

phrases.english: But let it atone
phrases.notes: Some versions say וְנִתְכַּפַּר and some say the word in square brackets, וּנְכַפַּר. Both mean about the same thing.

phrases.english: with complete atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit (suspension only) after step 6 confirmed the goat applies to this case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that the inner goat only suspends punishment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goat covers this sin at all, it should cover it fully.

steps.title: The wording 'for all their sins' means only suspension
steps.stepSummary: "מחטאתם" would have meant full atonement. "לכל חטאתם" means the goat is for sins that will later need a חטאת, so it only holds things off until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse said "from their sins," you would be right. Now that it says "for all their sins," it means sins that will come to need a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From their sins" would sound like the goat removes the sins completely. "For all their sins" points to sins that will later need a קרבן חטאת. So the goat cannot replace that קרבן; it only holds back the punishment until he brings it.

keyTerms.meaning: "From their sins" (wording that would mean full removal)
Into the category of a sin-offering

steps.whatToRemember: The inner goat only suspends punishment for someone who knew at the beginning but not at the end. He still brings his קרבן once he finds out.

phrases.english: If it were written: "From their sins,"
it would be as you say;
now that it is written: "For all their sins,"
it means those sins that come into the category of a sin-offering.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's wording
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of "לכל חטאתם," the goat only suspends the punishment until the person brings his חטאת.

steps.title: What good is suspending the punishment?
steps.stepSummary: If the goat does not truly atone, what does suspending accomplish?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since it does not atone, why does it suspend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical benefit the suspension gives. The next steps will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person will have to bring a קרבן anyway once he remembers. So what does he gain from the goat in the meantime?

keyTerms.meaning: Since, once it is so that
Atones

phrases.english: But since it does not atone,
why does it suspend?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר לָמָּה תּוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 8's conclusion that the goat only suspends.

steps.title: רבי זירא: if he dies, he dies without sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the benefit is that if he dies before bringing his קרבן, he dies free of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It means that if he dies, he dies without sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a first answer to the question of what the suspension does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suspension matters if the person never gets the chance to bring his קרבן. If he dies first, the goat has made sure he dies without this sin on him.

keyTerms.meaning: Without sin

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It means to say that if he dies,
he dies without sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לוֹמַר שֶׁאִם מֵת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The goat ensures that if he dies before bringing his קרבן, he dies free of sin.

steps.title: רבא: death itself already cleanses
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבי זירא's answer, because death atones anyway, so the goat would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If he dies, death itself cleanses!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death atones for a person's sins anyway. So if the goat's only job were to help someone who dies, it would accomplish nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Death cleanses (wipes away sin)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If he dies,
death cleanses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא אִם מֵת מִיתָה מְמָרֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי זירא's explanation of the purpose of suspension
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Death already atones, so the goat would serve no purpose in that case.

steps.title: רבא: the goat protects him from suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the suspension protects the person from יסורין until he brings his קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is to protect him from suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to what the suspension does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he is still alive and has not yet brought his קרבן, the person could be punished with suffering. The goat holds that back. This gives the suspension a real effect during his lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: To protect
Suffering (as a punishment)

steps.whatToRemember: Suspending punishment means the person is protected from suffering until he brings his קרבן, as רבא explains.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is to protect him from suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא לְהָגֵן עָלָיו מִן הַיִּסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי זירא's rejected answer with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suspension shields him from suffering until he brings his קרבן.

steps.title: The משנה's next case: awareness only at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: when there was no awareness at the beginning but there was awareness at the end, the outer goat and יום הכפורים atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was no awareness at the beginning but there was awareness at the end, the goat offered outside and יום הכפורים atone, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה. This sets up a new discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the focus was the inner goat and the person who knew at the beginning. Now the case changes: he knew only at the end. Here the outer goat (part of the מוספין) together with the day of יום הכפורים gives atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness at the beginning (knowing the facts before sinning)
Awareness at the end (finding out afterward)
The goat whose service is done outside the היכל, part of the מוספין
The Day of Atonement, which itself atones

phrases.english: There was no awareness at the beginning
but there was awareness at the end:
the goat that is done outside
and יום הכפורים atone, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the inner-goat discussion to the משנה's next case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For no awareness at the beginning but awareness at the end, the outer goat and יום הכפורים atone.

steps.title: Let the inner goat also cover the outer goat's cases
steps.stepSummary: Since the two goats are linked by a הקש, the גמרא asks why the inner שעיר shouldn't atone both for its own cases and for the outer שעיר's cases. That would matter when the outer goat was never brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, the two goats are linked to each other. So let the inner goat atone for its own cases and also for the outer goat's cases. The practical difference would be when the outer goat was not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the setup. If the two goats are linked, maybe the inner goat can do both jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הקש usually means two things share their laws. The גמרא pushes this further: if they share, the inner goat could take over the outer goat's work. This would make a real difference in a year when the outer goat was not brought for some reason.

keyTerms.meaning: They were linked (compared) to each other by the פסוק, a הקש
The inner goat, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל
The outer goat, the מוסף sin-offering brought outside
The practical difference

phrases.english: Now, they are linked to each other,
phrases.notes: "They" means the two goats of יום הכפורים, which the פסוק links together.

phrases.english: so let the inner one atone for its own cases and for the outer one's cases,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לְהֵיכָא דְּלָא עֲבַד חִיצוֹן!
phrases.english: and the difference would be where the outer one was not offered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the הקש between the two goats further, asking whether it lets the inner goat take over the outer goat's role.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that each goat covers only its own set of cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goats are linked by a הקש, their atoning power should be shared, so the inner goat should be able to cover the outer goat's cases too.

steps.title: The word 'once' limits a goat to one atonement
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "אחת" (once), which teaches that each goat atones for one kind of case only, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "once": it atones for one atonement, and it does not atone for two atonements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הקש shows the goats deal with similar kinds of sin. But the word "אחת" sets a limit: each goat does one job only. So the inner goat cannot add the outer goat's job to its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Once / one
Atonement

phrases.english: The verse says: "once",
it brings one atonement,
and it does not bring two atonements.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by limiting the inner goat with a word from the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקש might let the inner goat cover the outer goat's cases as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "אחת" teaches that each goat brings only one atonement, so the inner goat cannot cover two sets of cases.

steps.title: Let the outer goat also cover the inner goat's cases
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the opposite: let the outer שעיר atone for its own cases and also for the inner שעיר's cases. That would matter for טומאה that happened between the two goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let the outer goat atone for its own cases and also for what the inner goat covers. The difference would be a case of טומאה that happened between this goat and that goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question and challenges again, this time about the outer goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner goat is offered first, so it cannot help with טומאה that happens after it is done. If the outer goat could also do the inner goat's job, it would cover טומאה that happened between the two offerings. So the challenge asks why the outer goat shouldn't take over here.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own (cases)
Ritual impurity (here, entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure)
Between this one and that one (between the two goats)

phrases.english: But let the outer one atone for its own cases,
and for what the inner one does,
the difference would be for טומאה
that happened between this one and that one!
phrases.notes: Meaning after the inner goat was done but before the outer goat was offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 14 in the other direction, asking whether the outer goat can take on the inner goat's role.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the outer goat covers only its own cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the goats are linked, the later outer goat should also cover the inner goat's kind of case, which matters for טומאה that came after the inner goat was done.

steps.title: The words 'once a year' limit each atonement
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "אחת בשנה" (once a year). The גמרא begins to explain that this atonement should happen only once a year; the sentence finishes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "once a year": this atonement shall not be...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer from the words "אחת בשנה". The sentence is cut off here and finishes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner goat's kind of atonement is supposed to happen only once a year. If the outer goat also did it, that atonement would happen twice on the same day. So the extra words "בשנה" block the outer goat from taking over.

keyTerms.meaning: Once a year
This atonement (the specific one this goat brings)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. "אחת" stopped the inner goat from doing two jobs; "אחת בשנה" stops the outer goat from repeating the inner goat's job that same year.

phrases.english: The verse says: "once a year",
this atonement shall not be...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 with the fuller phrase "אחת בשנה" from the same פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer goat might also cover the inner goat's cases, such as טומאה that happened between the two goats.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אחת בשנה" teaches that this atonement happens only once a year, so the outer goat cannot repeat the inner goat's atonement.
